success_patterns: Use the canonical initial page or offset when retrieving a collection for the first time, even when the user does not explicitly say “first page.”
Keep initial-position parameters distinct from result limits; do not invent a count for a request that does not specify one.

patch.reasoning: Several trajectories retrieve an initial collection or screen and omit its documented starting position: paginated match and character lists, and stock screens with a start index. A narrowly scoped rule fills that gap while avoiding unsupported limits, as illustrated by the Medium request where no result count was specified.

edits.target: When the user explicitly requests the first page, pass `page=1` on every applicable paginated call; do the same where applicable when a requested count is served by a paginated endpoint.
edits.content: When the user explicitly requests the first page, pass `page=1` on every applicable paginated call. Also use the canonical initial position for an initial collection retrieval when the endpoint exposes a documented or unambiguous page/index convention (for example, `page=1` for one-based pages or `start=0`/`offset=0` for zero-based indexes), even if the user does not say “first page.” Do not confuse an offset with a page number or invent a result limit. When a requested count is served by a paginated endpoint, map it to the documented count or page-size field.
